events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
The trip was a non-metered RydeX fixed-fare ride: the rider was quoted and billed $25.04, and the billed distance is exactly the 10.8 km optimal-route distance [F4][F5][F6][RD-2]. The rider's recollection that "the meter came to 11 km" is contradicted by the fare record, and system records override the complaint, so no extra distance was billed [F4][F6][RD-2].

On the route itself, there is one off-route segment, 14:19–14:22, in which 2.15 km were driven where the optimal route covers 1.38 km, adding 0.77 km and reaching up to 1019 m from the optimal route [F3][RD-1]. This segment was preceded by no driver request and no rider agreement — there are zero in-app chat messages — so RD-5 consent is unavailable [F7][RD-5]. The driver's "my GPS rerouted me" statement is an after-the-fact explanation and does not satisfy RD-5 [F8][RD-5].

No RD-4 reasonable-cause exemption applies: no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, and the only traffic records are band 4 (30–39 km/h) speed bands on the AYE and CTE [F9][F10][F11][RD-4]. Band 4 is far above the band 1–2 congestion reference, and band evidence cannot exempt a segment on its own [F9][F10][RD-4].

Applying RD-2's non-metered branch: because the fare is a fixed quote unaffected by mileage [F4][F5][F6][RD-2], the only recoverable items are ERP/toll incurred on the unexempted segment and any unpublished post-trip add-ons [F6][RD-2][FARE-1]. The itemised charge contains only published components — base $3.90, distance $15.17 (10.8 km), time $4.50, waiting $0.00, platform $1.47 — and no toll or unpublished item [F6][FARE-1], so the refundable amount is $0.00 and the fare stands [F6][RD-2].

Because the RD-1 breach is nonetheless established on an unexempted segment [F3][RD-1], and the driver's profile shows 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, making this a repeated breach [F14][RD-6], the account-review flag attaches as an add-on action; the profile is used only for that additional action, not to decide the substantive finding [F14][RD-6].

actions.detail: account action is never automatic; queued for Ryde review

what_would_change: Had an LTA incident been recorded on the stretch F3 replaced, before it started, RD-4 would exempt it (−$0.00).

claims.assertion: The GPS track shows the driver added 1.6 km over the optimal route (12.4 km actual vs 10.8 km optimal), and one off-route segment at 14:19–14:22 added 0.77 km, reaching 1019 m from the optimal route — an unexplained deviation from the shortest and most direct route.
There is no in-app chat agreement at all: the chat record contains no messages between rider and driver, so the rider never consented to the route change before the driver left the optimal route.

The driver's excuse that 'my GPS rerouted me' is not a policy defence: the only accepted justification for a reroute is a traffic fact tied to the replaced optimal-route segment, and the traffic records show no incidents near the route during the trip window; only moderate speed bands 4 (30–39 km/h) appear, which do not qualify.

Because the trip is a non-metered RydeX fixed-fare ride, the extra kilometres do not raise the fare; the billed distance is exactly the optimal 10.8 km (no excess) and there is no surge, so the only recoverable items are the extra ERP/toll incurred on the unexempted segment and any unpublished add-ons.

No unpublished charge was added: the $25.04 total is base $3.90 + distance $15.17 + time $4.50 + platform $1.47, with waiting $0.00, so nothing beyond the quoted fixed fare plus published components was levied and the refundable monetary amount computes to $0.00.
The driver has 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days and this case makes a third, so an account review flag is warranted alongside the finding that RD-1 was breached.

weaknesses: The monetary recovery is zero on this fare model: F4 shows the billed distance (10.8 km) equals the optimal route, and F6 shows a fixed $25.04 with waiting $0.00 — so the rider's request to 'refund the extra distance' cannot be quantified from any fare or GPS fact, and RD-2's non-metered branch refunds only extra ERP/toll, for which the dataset has no tolls fact.

The rider's own complaint says 'the meter came to 11 km', which the system records contradict: F1 gives 12.4 km actual and F4 gives 10.8 km billed, so the rider's recollection of being billed extra distance is not supported.

The deviation was mild — 0.77 km on the single off-route segment and +1.6 min total (F2, F3) — so the driver will argue it was a trivial GPS reroute rather than a deliberate detour, and F8 asserts exactly that.

The weather was fair (F12) and traffic showed no incidents (F11), which cuts against the driver's congestion excuse but equally means there is no dramatic harm to point to, weakening any argument for a large remedy.

claims.assertion: This is a RydeX (non-metered) trip: the fare was a fixed quote of $25.04 and the billed distance is exactly the quoted 10.8 km, so the extra 1.6 km of actual driving did not increase the fare at all.

Under RD-2, the non-metered branch of the remedy is limited to ERP/toll and unpublished post-trip add-ons; the fare breakdown shows no toll or unpublished item — only base, distance, time, platform fee and $0.00 waiting — so the refundable amount on the fare is $0.

Only one off-route segment exists (14:19–14:22, adding 0.77 km), and it is not exempt: it added distance while the fastest available roads were only moderately slow (band 4, 30–39 km/h) and no incident was recorded, so no RD-4 exemption applies to it.

The driver did not obtain the rider's agreement before leaving the optimal route: there is no in-app chat at all, so there is no rider consent message timestamped before the segment start at 14:19, and the driver's account ('I followed my GPS') is only an after-the-fact explanation.
The rider's own complaint that 'the meter came to 11 km' is contradicted by the fare record, which bills 10.8 km; the system record governs, so the complainant's distance premise fails.

Although RD-1 was breached on the unexempted 0.77 km segment, the corresponding refund is $0, so the correct disposition of the disputed charge is no_action; the breach is merely recorded against the driver.

weaknesses: The driver did breach the RD-1 shortest-and-most-direct-route duty: F3 records a 0.77 km off-route segment (14:19–14:22) that the rider never agreed to, and F7 shows zero chat, so RD-5 consent is unavailable; this breach is recorded against my client even if no money moves.

F1 (12.4 km actual vs 10.8 km optimal, +1.6 km / +15%) and F2 (+1.6 min) corroborate the rider's narrative of a longer-than-optimal drive, and a judge may weigh that perception against my 'fare unchanged' argument.

The rider has a clean 90-day record (F13: 0 upheld of 2 disputes), so the adjudicator will not discount the complaint as vexatious, whereas my client's F14 shows 2 upheld route disputes in 90 d — on the rider's side this would support an added flag_account under RD-6, and it cuts against my client's credibility on route choice.

points.response: Conceded on the arithmetic: F4 bills exactly 10.8 km and F6 shows a fixed $25.04, so the 1.6 km of extra driving did not raise the fare — but that concession only fixes the size of the money claim, not whether RD-1 was breached.

Agreed that the non-metered branch of RD-2 limits the refund to ERP/toll and unpublished post-trip charges, and F6 shows none; I therefore no longer press a dollar figure, but RD-2's $0 branch still requires the RD-1 violation to be recorded against the driver.

The driver concedes the segment is unexempt, and the traffic facts confirm it: F11 records no incident near the route and F9/F10 show only band 4 (30–39 km/h), which falls far short of the band 1–2 congestion RD-4 requires, so no reasonable cause exists for the 0.77 km added by F3.

No dispute: F7 shows zero in-app messages, so there was no rider agreement before the 14:19 segment start, and F8's 'my GPS rerouted me' is exactly the after-the-fact explanation RD-5 excludes — a finding that the driver violated RD-1 by not taking the shortest and most direct route.

I withdraw the rider's '11 km' premise: F4 and F6 show 10.8 km billed, and I accept the system record governs — but the same records prove the deviation occurred (F1: 12.4 km actual, F3: one off-route segment), so the premise fails without the breach failing.

We agree on no_action for the money, but we do not agree the record stops there: F14 shows 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days and this is a third unexempted deviation, which under RD-6 makes the case 'repeated' and requires the additional flag_account the rider asks for, alongside the recorded RD-1 breach.

Conceded with a qualification: F3 does establish one off-route segment (14:19–14:22, +0.77 km) that my client cannot justify, but F1's headline figure of +1.6 km total actual distance is not itself a policy threshold — RD-1 turns on unexplained off-route segments, and RD-2 limits any remedy on a fixed-fare RydeX trip to extra ERP/toll and unpublished add-ons.

Conceded: F7 shows no in-app messages at all, so there is no rider consent timestamped before the segment start at 14:19 and RD-5 cannot exempt the segment; my client's explanation in F8 was given only after the fact.

Accepted on the traffic point, but note that F8 is not the basis of my defence — even granting the RD-4 argument entirely, F9/F10 show only band 4 (30–39 km/h) and F11 shows no incidents, so the failure to exempt the segment changes the remedy under RD-2, which remains $0 on this fare model.

This is my own D2 position and the decisive point: F4 shows the billed distance equals the 10.8 km optimal route and F5 shows no surge, so under RD-2's non-metered branch the rider has no extra-distance sum to recover and no toll fact exists to refund.

Agreed: F6 itemises only published components (base $3.90, distance $15.17, time $4.50, platform $1.47, waiting $0.00), so FARE-1 yields no unpublished item to refund and the rider's monetary recovery is $0.00.

F14 shows 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, so the RD-6 flag_account is a natural consequence of the recorded RD-1 breach and my client does not contest an account review; it is an add-on action, not a money award, and RD-6 prohibits using the profile to decide the substantive finding.

Withdrawing my D5 only to the extent it reads as a substantive defence: it remains true that F4/F6 show 10.8 km billed, disproving the rider's '11 km' recollection, but that does not excuse my client's off-route segment under RD-1.
